name: Gootloader
desc: Attack flow on the Gootloader payload distribution attack.

acts.d: Attackers compromised websites to host malware

The user searched for results and clicked on a compromised website. After navigating to the compromised website, a forum-looking page was displayed and the user clicked on a link, which downloaded a file
The user double clicked on the dropped zip file
User double-clicks Javascript file, located within zip, to execute
Gootloader creates two registry keys, the first is populated with an encoded Cobalt Strike payload and the latter stores a .NET loader
A PowerShell command is issued to extract the .NET loader from the registry and executes the code in memory via Assembly.Load()
The encoded PowerShell script creates a Scheduled Task that executes when the user logs on to the computer.
.NET loader decodes a Cobalt Strike payload from the registry and loads and executes the payload
The threat actors used Bloodhound on the initial victim computer to enumerate the Active Directory domain
The threat actors used Bloodhound on the initial victim computer to enumerate the Active Directory domain
The threat actors used Bloodhound on the initial victim computer to enumerate the Active Directory domain
The attackers then pivoted to nearby workstation host via a Cobalt Strike Powershell beacon
Attackers disabled Windows Defender logs on the Workstation
A second Cobalt Strike payload is deployed on the workstation to initiate a second C2 server
WMI used to check for AV software on the 2 compromised computers
checks for AV software on the 2 compromised computers
The malicious PowerShell process used by Gootloader dropped a PowerShell script on the file system.
Another PowerShell command triggers the mi.ps1 script on the initial victim's computer to harvest credentials
The threat actors then ran LaZagne to retrieve all saved credentials from the workstation
The attackers enabled Restricted Admin Mode through remote WMI. This was allowed because RAM only requires knowledge of the password hash, not the cleartext password
Using the harvested credentials, the threat actors used RDP to move from the initial victim computer to the compromised workstation in restricted admin mode.
Microsoft Defender Scheduled Tasks Deleted
SMB was used to transfer Cobalt Strike payload executables to 3 additional workstations.
